title: While Some in Folly's Pleasures Roll
description: While Some in Folly's Pleasures Roll in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Nathaniel Cotton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 432 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “A Peaceful Conscience”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: While some in fol-ly's plea-sures roll, And court the joys that hurt the soul, Be mine that si-lent, calm re-past, A con-science peace-ful to the last.

lines: While some in folly's pleasures roll,
And court the joys that hurt the soul,
Be mine that silent, calm repast,
A conscience peaceful to the last.
With this companion in the shade,
My soul no more shall be dismayed;
But fearless meet life's dreariest gloom,
And the pale monarch of the tomb.
Amidst the various scenes of ills,
Each blow some kind design fulfils;
And can I murmur at my God,
While love supreme directs the rod?
His hand will smooth my rugged way,
And lead me to the realms of day;
To milder skies, and brighter plains,

licence: Public domain: Nathaniel Cotton died in 1788.
credits: Words by Nathaniel Cotton (1705–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
